q: גבר בן 73 ,שמור קוגניטיבית, שנתיים לאחר אירוע מוחי עם חולשת פלג גוף ימין, פנה למלר\"ד בעקבות נפילה וחבלה לאגן. עד הנפילה התהלך עם הליכון. בצילום רנטגן: מה הטיפול המומלץ לפי המאמר Management of Acute Hip Fracture ?
o: רדוקציה של השבר בחדר ניתוח והשכבה עם מתיחה ל- 3 שבועות
ניתוח arthroplasty, תוך עד 48 שעות מהנפילה, וניוד מוקדם
בשל מגבלת ניידות מלפני הנפילה מומלץ להימנע מניתוח, מומלצת פיזיותרפיה וניוד מוקדם ככל האפשר
ניתוח מיסמור תוך לשדי (intramedullary nails)
explanation:
Official answer: ב

**Official answer:** arthroplasty within 48 hours of the fall and early mobilization (IMA final key, 2020, question 25). The textbook supports arthroplasty for a displaced femoral-neck fracture and weight bearing as tolerated after repair, supporting the operation and mobilization principles (Hazzard, p. 794).

**A. Reduce the fracture in theatre, then bed rest with traction for 3 weeks.** Wrong, weeks in traction do not deliver the recommended operative repair and conflict with the article’s emphasis on early mobilization (NEJM, pp. 2057, 2060).
**B. Arthroplasty within 48 hours and early mobilization.** Correct, the image shows a displaced femoral-neck fracture. Arthroplasty is appropriate in this age group, and impaired prior ambulation points toward hemiarthroplasty in the algorithm. The article supports surgery within 48 hours and early mobilization (NEJM, pp. 2055–2057, 2060).
**C. Avoid surgery because of prior mobility limitations; use physiotherapy and early mobilization.** Wrong, previous walking-frame use alone does not justify avoiding surgery; the algorithm explicitly includes arthroplasty for limited ambulation (NEJM, p. 2056).
**D. Intramedullary nails.** Wrong, the algorithm uses these for unstable intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric fractures, whereas this film shows a displaced femoral-neck fracture (NEJM, pp. 2055–2056).

The official image (2020 paper, p. 8) is Figure 2B of the article, a displaced femoral-neck fracture. For a 73-year-old walking-frame user, the article’s algorithm supports arthroplasty, with hemiarthroplasty for limited ambulation. Surgery within 48 hours of the event and early mobilization complete the officially accepted combination (NEJM, pp. 2055–2057, 2059–2060, Figures 2–3).

Source: Bhandari and Swiontkowski. Management of Acute Hip Fracture. NEJM 2017, pp. 2055–2057, 2059–2060; Hazzard 8e, p. 794; IMA 2020 paper, p. 8.

q: בן 75, ברקע - מחלת לב איסכמית, MI לפני כ-5 שנים, מטופל ב- ASPIRIN. התקבל לאשפוז בעקבות דלקת ריאות. במהלך האשפוז, בעקבות פרפור פרוזדורים עם תגובה חדרית של 120, טופל בחוסמי ביטא וחזר לקצב סינוס. המטופל במשקל 70 ק"ג, בד"כ נייד בבית, נפל לפני כחצי שנה בביתו בעקבות היתקלות בשטיח, תפקודי כליה תקינים. מהו הטיפול התרופתי המומלץ בשחרורו?
o: הוספת טיפול ב- APIXABAN 2.5mg (ELIQUIS) פעמיים ביום
הפסקת טיפול ב-ASPIRIN והתחלת טיפול ב-APIXABAN 5mg (ELIQUIS) פעמיים ביום
הוספת טיפול ב-RIVAROXABAN 15mg (XARELTO) פעם ביום
המשך טיפול ב ASPIRIN בלבד
explanation:
**Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation** requires an anticoagulant and dose appropriate to thromboembolic risk and renal function; aspirin is not a substitute when anticoagulation is indicated. In stable coronary disease without a history of stent thrombosis, the guideline favors anticoagulation alone over combination with aspirin to reduce major bleeding (Joglar et al., sections 6.3.1 and 6.8.2).

**A. Addition of apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily.** Wrong, the stated age, weight, and renal function do not justify the reduced dose. Dosing follows the criteria rather than automatic reduction for older age or one fall (Hazzard 8e, p. 1205, Table 77-9).
**B. Discontinuation of aspirin and initiation of apixaban 5 mg twice daily.** Correct, this combines the usual apixaban dose with aspirin discontinuation in stable coronary disease. A remote infarction alone does not justify continued combination treatment. This application assumes no additional antiplatelet indication or history of stent thrombosis omitted from the stem (p. 1205; Joglar et al., section 6.8.2).
**C. Addition of rivaroxaban 15 mg once daily.** Wrong, this is a renal-adjusted dose, whereas renal function is described as normal; addition to aspirin also does not match the preferred stable-coronary-disease regimen without another indication (p. 1204; Joglar et al., section 6.8.2).
**D. Continuation of aspirin alone.** Wrong, aspirin is not an adequate substitute for anticoagulation in AF with thromboembolic risk warranting treatment. Return to sinus rhythm alone does not remove the need for risk assessment (Joglar et al., sections 6.2 and 6.3.1).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1204-1205; Joglar et al., 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS atrial fibrillation guideline, sections 6.2, 6.3.1 and 6.8.2; doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2023.08.017. Same guideline checked in its parallel Circulation author manuscript, PDF pp. 30-34, 53.

q: A 75-year-old woman has mixed urinary incontinence with both stress and urgency symptoms. Frequent urgency-related leakage bothers her much more than occasional stress leakage. Her postvoid residual is normal. Which initial treatment priority is appropriate?
o: Prioritize a surgical intervention for the stress component
Prioritize nonsurgical treatment for the stress component
Prioritize initial treatment for the urgency component
Give both components equal priority at the start of treatment
explanation:
In **mixed incontinence**, initial treatment is directed by the symptoms that bother the patient most. Hazzard states, "Treatment of mixed incontinence should initially target the symptoms the individual finds most bothersome" (p. 714). Applying that rule here identifies urgency-related leakage as the initial target.

**A. Prioritize a surgical intervention for the stress component.** Wrong, this prioritizes the less bothersome symptom; stress surgery is considered for women unresponsive to nonsurgical treatment, which is not established here (p. 714).
**B. Prioritize nonsurgical treatment for the stress component.** Wrong, this also prioritizes stress leakage despite the patient identifying urgency as the greater problem (p. 714).
**C. Prioritize initial treatment for the urgency component.** Correct, urgency is the symptom she finds most bothersome, matching the stated treatment priority (p. 714).
**D. Give both components equal priority at the start of treatment.** Wrong, equal initial priority misses the source's instruction to target the more bothersome symptoms first in this situation (p. 714).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 714.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 714, Mixed incontinence

q: אישה בת 80 עם דמנציה קלה, HTN, ו-UTIs חוזרים, גרה לבד. בנה מוצא אותה מבולבלת עם בגדים מלוכלכים במהלך ביקור. היא מאושפזת עם urosepsis, E. coli bacteremia, ו-AKI (Cr 2.8, baseline 1.0). לאחר טיפול, היא יציבה מבחינה רפואית אך מקבלת 18/30 ב-MMSE וזקוקה להשגחה לתרופות ולהיגיינה. הבן עובד במהלך היום. מתחיל תכנון שחרור. איזו אפשרות מאזנת בצורה הטובה ביותר בין האוטונומיה שלה לצרכי הבטיחות?
o: שחרור לבית עם home health aide יומי
הרשמה ל-PACE program עם נוכחות ב-day center
אשפוז קבוע בבית אבות
מעבר לגור עם הבן ו-adult day care
explanation:
התשובה הנכונה היא הרשמה ל-PACE. היא הדגימה חוסר יכולת לתפקד באופן עצמאי (הזנחת היגיינה שהובילה ל-infection חמור) אך עשויה להישאר בקהילה עם תמיכה מקיפה. PACE מספקת השגחה יומית דרך day center, ניהול תרופות, סיוע בטיפול אישי, וניהול רפואי פרואקטיבי למניעת UTIs עתידיים.

אפשרות A (בית עם aide) היא המלכודת — שומרת על עצמאות אך מספקת השגחה לא מספקת. ביקורי aide יומיים משאירים שעות רבות ללא השגחה, ו-aides אינם יכולים לנהל תרופות או לספק monitoring רפואי.

אפשרות C (בית אבות) היא מוקדמת מדי — היא אינה ברמת תלות של בית אבות ועשויה לשגשג עם תמיכה קהילתית מתאימה. institutionalization לרוב מאיץ את ה-cognitive decline.

אפשרות D (גרה עם הבן) משבשת את חייהם של שניהם, ו-day care אינו מתמודד עם ניהול תרופות או המורכבות הרפואית. כמו כן אינה מספקת כיסוי בערב/סוף שבוע כשהבן נמצא בבית.

Clinical Pearl: משתתפי PACE עם דמנציה נשארים בסביבה קהילתית פי 3 יותר מנהנים מסורתיים של Medicare. גורמים מרכזיים כוללים פרוטוקולי מניעת UTI פרואקטיביים (סיוע בהיגיינה, monitoring הידרציה, טיפול מהיר) והשגחה יומית המונעת משברים המובילים ל-institutionalization.
ref: Hazzard Ch 17 — COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE
chapterTitle: COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: אישה בת 79 במוסד סיעודי מפתחת דלקת ריאות אספירטיבית חוזרת. יש לה דמנציה וסקולרית בינונית (MMSE 18/30), סוכרת, ו-CKD שלב 3 (eGFR 45). התרופות הנוכחיות כוללות metformin 500 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg ליום, ו-sertraline 50 mg ליום. בדיקת בליעה בווידאופלואורוסקופיה מראה אספירציה שקטה של נוזלים דקים. קלינאית התקשורת ממליצה על נוזלים מסומכים, אך המטופלת מסרבת. לבתה יש ייפוי כוח מתמשך. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?
o: הנחת PEG tube לכל התזונה
דחיית סירוב המטופלת ואכיפת נוזלים מסומכים
דיון במטרות טיפול ובעדיפויות איכות החיים
הפסקת כל צריכה אורלית באופן מיידי
explanation:
**הזנה בדמנציה** מחייבת החלטה פרטנית על דרך מתן המזון והנוזלים, תוך הערכת בליעה וצרכים תזונתיים. ההמלצות הישראליות מעדיפות הזנה דרך הפה, וחוק זכויות החולה מחייב מידע על התועלת, הסיכון והחלופות לצורך הסכמה. לכן בירור **מטרות הטיפול ואיכות החיים** הוא הסקה יישומית המתאימה לסירוב המתואר, לפני בחירה חד צדדית בדרך הזנה (המלצות הוועדה, עמ׳ 5; סעיף 13).
"הדרך המועדפת למתן המזון והנוזלים היא דרך הפה." (המלצות הוועדה, עמ׳ 5)

**א. הנחת PEG tube לכל התזונה.** שגויה, מעבר אוטומטי להזנה דרך צינור אינו ההחלטה הפרטנית שההמלצות דורשות. יש לשקול דרך הזנה בהתאם למצב, לצרכים ולהערכת הבליעה, ולא להסיק אותה מעצם הסירוב להסמכה (עמ׳ 5; סעיף 13).
**ב. דחיית סירוב המטופלת ואכיפת נוזלים מסומכים.** שגויה, ההצעה עוקפת את בירור הסירוב וההסכמה. עצם קיומו של ייפוי כוח בשאלה אינו מתאר החלטה מוסכמת על כפיית נוזלים מסומכים; יש לברר הבנה ורצון לפני פעולה (יישום סעיף 13).
**ג. דיון ב-goals of care ובעדיפויות איכות החיים.** נכונה, דיון כזה מאפשר להבין את הסירוב ולשקול את בטיחות הבליעה מול מטרות המטופלת והחלופות. הוא מקדם החלטה פרטנית על ההזנה ומידע הנדרש להסכמה (הסקה מעמ׳ 5 וסעיף 13).
**ד. הפסקת כל צריכה אורלית באופן מיידי.** שגויה, הפסקת כל צריכה פומית אינה מסקנה אוטומטית מן הממצא לגבי נוזלים דקים. המקור דורש הערכה מקצועית והתאמה פרטנית של מתן מזון ונוזלים, ולא החלטה גורפת ללא בירור נוסף (עמ׳ 5).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8 בקובץ המקומי. המלצות הוועדה להזנה בחולים עם קיהיון, עמ׳ 5.

q: A 78-year-old woman develops postoperative delirium. She receives diphenhydramine for sleep and famotidine started during admission; neither has an ongoing essential indication. According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which medication-review approach is appropriate?
o: Consider stopping both drugs to reduce medication-related delirium risk
Consider retaining both drugs and adding lorazepam at night
Consider retaining diphenhydramine and adding zolpidem for sleep
Consider retaining famotidine and adding clonazepam at night
explanation:
**Medication review in delirium** includes both anticholinergics and H2-receptor antagonists. The Beers Criteria advise avoiding listed drugs in older adults with or at high risk of delirium "because of the potential of inducing or worsening delirium" (p. 2066). Diphenhydramine is listed as strongly anticholinergic (p. 2074).

**A. Consider stopping both drugs to reduce medication-related delirium risk.** Correct, both medications fall within the listed delirium-risk categories; reviewing discontinuation fits the absence of an ongoing essential indication (pp. 2066, 2074).
**B. Consider retaining both drugs and adding lorazepam at night.** Wrong, this retains the two risk medications and adds a benzodiazepine, another category listed for avoidance in delirium (p. 2066).
**C. Consider retaining diphenhydramine and adding zolpidem for sleep.** Wrong, this retains an anticholinergic and adds zolpidem, which is also listed for avoidance in delirium (pp. 2066, 2074).
**D. Consider retaining famotidine and adding clonazepam at night.** Wrong, this retains an H2-receptor antagonist and adds a benzodiazepine; both categories appear in the delirium criterion (p. 2066).

Source: AGS Beers 2023, pp. 2066, 2074.

q: An 82-year-old man with mild dementia and treated depression has acquired a firearm for protection. His wife recently found him looking sad while holding the loaded gun. He denies suicidal thoughts and says he was checking the weapon. He takes sertraline and donepezil. Alongside immediate assessment of suicide risk, which action directly reduces access to lethal means?
o: Increase the antidepressant dose and arrange a later follow-up visit
Arrange a mental-health referral while leaving firearm access unchanged
Document firearm-storage advice while leaving firearm access unchanged
Work with family to remove access to the firearm temporarily
explanation:
**Reducing access to lethal means** is an immediate risk-reduction measure, alongside assessment of intent, planning, and available means. Hazzard states that "removing the firearm or other means can decrease immediate risk" (p. 1018). It describes involving someone in the patient’s life to help decrease access; applying that principle here does not establish intent or rule out the need for hospitalization.

**A. Increase the antidepressant dose and arrange a later follow-up visit.** Wrong, a dose change and later review do not reduce the immediate availability of the firearm, the specific risk addressed by the source passage (p. 1018).
**B. Arrange a mental-health referral while leaving firearm access unchanged.** Wrong, specialist referral may be needed, but leaving the weapon accessible does not implement the immediate means-reduction measure (p. 1018).
**C. Document firearm-storage advice while leaving firearm access unchanged.** Wrong, documentation and advice do not accomplish removal of access if the firearm remains available (p. 1018; application).
**D. Work with family to remove access to the firearm temporarily.** Correct, this enlists support to reduce actual access while the clinical risk assessment and further care proceed (p. 1018).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1018.

q: A 75-year-old man with symptomatic lumbar spinal stenosis asks about epidural steroid injection. Which result matches the randomized trial in Hazzard comparing glucocorticoid plus lidocaine with lidocaine injection?
o: Little added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection
Substantial added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection
Little added short-term benefit compared with an uninjected control
Substantial added short-term benefit compared with decompressive surgery
explanation:
**The comparator defines the conclusion** of this trial. Hazzard reports “minimal or no short-term benefit in outcomes (disability and leg pain intensity)” from adding glucocorticoid to lidocaine (p. 1639). Because the comparison was with lidocaine injection and there was no placebo group, this trial does not establish effects against no injection or against surgery (p. 1639).

**A. Little added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection.** Correct, it preserves both the actual comparator and the reported short-term result for disability and leg pain (p. 1639).
**B. Substantial added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection.** Wrong, the reported added benefit was minimal or absent, not substantial (p. 1639).
**C. Little added short-term benefit compared with an uninjected control.** Wrong, there was no uninjected or placebo control; both described groups received an injection (p. 1639).
**D. Substantial added short-term benefit compared with decompressive surgery.** Wrong, the comparison was between two injection regimens, not injection versus decompressive surgery (p. 1639).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1639.
ref: Hazzard Ch 102 — BACK PAIN AND SPINAL STENOSIS

q: An 81-year-old woman with diabetes receives insulin and a beta-blocker for cardiovascular disease. Which beta-blocker effect is relevant to hypoglycemia safety?
o: It may enhance the counterregulatory response to falling blood glucose
It may impair the counterregulatory response to falling blood glucose
It may strengthen adrenergic counterregulation during a fall in glucose
It may preserve adrenergic counterregulation during a fall in glucose
explanation:
**Counterregulation** helps raise blood glucose during hypoglycemia. Hazzard notes that beta-adrenergic blockers can interfere with this response and advises avoiding their combination with insulin or a sulfonylurea when alternatives are possible (p. 1584).
"β-adrenergic blocking drugs can potentially interfere with counterregulation of hypoglycemia." (p. 1584).
"Given the substantial benefit of β-adrenergic blockade to patients with CVD, combination with insulin or a sulfonylurea should be avoided and other glucose-lowering drugs used if possible." (p. 1584).

**A. It may enhance the counterregulatory response to falling blood glucose.** Wrong, the described effect is interference with the response, not enhancement (p. 1584).
**B. It may impair the counterregulatory response to falling blood glucose.** Correct, the source specifically identifies potential interference with counterregulation of hypoglycemia (p. 1584).
**C. It may strengthen adrenergic counterregulation during a fall in glucose.** Wrong, beta-adrenergic blockade can interfere with this response; strengthened adrenergic counterregulation does not match the stated effect (p. 1584).
**D. It may preserve adrenergic counterregulation during a fall in glucose.** Wrong, the source warns that beta blockade can interfere with counterregulation, so preservation is not the effect identified by the passage (p. 1584).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1584.

q: A 77-year-old woman presents after a fall and reports a month of dizziness on standing. She takes amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, and lisinopril 20 mg each morning. Blood pressure is 138/78 supine and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 68 to 74. Potassium is 3.3 and creatinine 1.2. During medication review, which option both removes the thiazide exposure associated with potassium loss and provides potassium replacement?
o: Move all three antihypertensives to bedtime without changing the prescribed drugs
Stop hydrochlorothiazide and provide potassium replacement with repeat monitoring
Reduce all three antihypertensive doses without providing potassium replacement
Replace lisinopril with an ARB while continuing the other prescribed drugs
explanation:
**Thiazide-associated hypokalemia** is a relevant medication concern. Hazzard identifies hypokalemia among common thiazide adverse effects and describes oral potassium replacement with repeat measurements (pp. 1225, 1270). "The most common adverse drug events are metabolic abnormalities, especially hypokalemia" (p. 1225).

**A. Move all three antihypertensives to bedtime without changing the prescribed drugs.** Wrong, changing administration time retains the thiazide exposure and does not provide potassium replacement (pp. 1225, 1270).
**B. Stop hydrochlorothiazide and provide potassium replacement with repeat monitoring.** Correct, this removes the identified thiazide and replaces potassium; repeat measurements are part of the source's replacement approach (pp. 1225, 1270).
**C. Reduce all three antihypertensive doses without providing potassium replacement.** Wrong, dose reduction leaves thiazide exposure in place and does not provide the replacement specified in the question (pp. 1225, 1270).
**D. Replace lisinopril with an ARB while continuing the other prescribed drugs.** Wrong, changing the renin–angiotensin drug retains hydrochlorothiazide and does not provide the specified potassium replacement (pp. 1225, 1270).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1225, 1270.

q: An independently mobile 81-year-old man has mild to moderate chronic constipation despite lifestyle changes. He drinks adequate fluids, has no suspected fecal impaction or obstruction, and has not tried laxatives. Which initial treatment fits the Hazzard stepwise approach?
o: Start daily oral docusate and review the bowel response
Start psyllium with fluids and review the bowel response
Start oral magnesium citrate and review the bowel response
Start daily enema treatment and review the bowel response
explanation:
**A bulk laxative** is the initial pharmacologic step for an ambulatory older person in the Hazzard approach. The source states: "In ambulatory older patients with chronic constipation, a daily bulk laxative is appropriate for both rectal outlet delay and slow-transit constipation" (p. 1378). Table 87-11 specifies psyllium with fluids and separates this pathway from treatment of fecal impaction (p. 1378).

**A. Start daily oral docusate and review the bowel response.** Wrong, Docusate is not supported as effective treatment for constipation or rectal outlet delay in older people (p. 1376).
**B. Start psyllium with fluids and review the bowel response.** Correct, Psyllium with fluids matches the initial step for ambulatory older people, and the stem provides adequate fluid intake (p. 1378).
**C. Start oral magnesium citrate and review the bowel response.** Wrong, Magnesium citrate is not recommended in older people because of its adverse-effect risk, including colonic pseudo-obstruction (p. 1376).
**D. Start daily enema treatment and review the bowel response.** Wrong, daily enemas appear in the disimpaction pathway, whereas this patient has uncomplicated chronic constipation and no suspected impaction (p. 1378).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1376, 1378.

q: An 81-year-old woman with hyponatremia takes a thiazide and sertraline. Which approach to medication review follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Consider the thiazide contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency
Consider both medications and monitor sodium when treatment is changed
Consider the sertraline contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency
Consider the combination protective and continue treatment without sodium monitoring
explanation:
**Diuretics and SSRIs** appear among drugs that may cause or exacerbate SIADH or hyponatremia. The Beers Criteria recommend caution and close sodium monitoring when initiating these drugs or changing doses; the list does not establish which drug caused an individual patient's low sodium (p. 2068).
"May exacerbate or cause SIADH or hyponatremia; monitor sodium levels closely when starting or changing dosages in older adults." (p. 2068).

**A. Consider the thiazide contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency.** Wrong, considering a diuretic contribution is appropriate, but reduced monitoring conflicts with the recommendation (p. 2068).
**B. Consider both medications and monitor sodium when treatment is changed.** Correct, both drug classes are listed, and closer monitoring during treatment changes matches the recommendation (p. 2068).
**C. Consider the sertraline contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency.** Wrong, considering an SSRI contribution is appropriate, but reduced monitoring conflicts with the recommendation (p. 2068).
**D. Consider the combination protective and continue treatment without sodium monitoring.** Wrong, both classes can contribute to hyponatremia; the source does not describe the combination as protective (p. 2068).

Source: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2068.

q: איזה מבין ההיגדים הבאים נכון באשר ליעילות הטיפול התרופתי בדיכאון בזקנים?
o: יעילות הטיפול התרופתי בחולים הלוקים בדמנציה מוטלת בספק
יעילות הטיפול בפלצבו זניחה בקרב מטופלים זקנים
יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר בקרב המאובחנים עם דיכאון קל לעומת דיכאון חמור
יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר ככל שהטיטרציה במינון מהירה יותר
explanation:
In patients with **dementia and depression**, antidepressant benefit is questionable after many negative trials. Assess measurable benefit rather than continuing treatment simply because it has already been prescribed (p. 1015).

**A. Drug-treatment efficacy in patients with dementia is questionable.** Correct, the source summarizes this conclusion after many negative studies (p. 1015).
**B. Placebo efficacy is negligible in older patients.** Wrong, placebo responses can be substantial, especially in less severe depression (p. 1014).
**C. Drug treatment is more effective in mild than severe depression.** Wrong, there is no evidence of benefit in mild or subthreshold depression; benefit beyond placebo is described mainly in more severe cases (pp. 1014-1015).
**D. Faster dose titration improves drug-treatment efficacy.** Wrong, starting low and titrating gradually was associated with better adherence even at the same eventual dose. The source proposes fewer adverse effects and more individualized attention as possible explanations, rather than an advantage from faster titration (p. 1015).

Gradual titration's association with adherence does not mean reaching the target faster guarantees greater efficacy (p. 1015). The placebo effect may be substantial, especially in less severe depression; the page does not provide the numerical range stated in an earlier explanation (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014-1015.
